overview.overviewText: This chapter explores Gay-Lussac\'s Law and Avogadro Hypothesis, providing comprehensive conceptual analysis, mathematical relationships, and structured applications grounded in NCERT authority.

blocks.title: 1. Key Academic Principles: Gay-Lussac\'s Law and Avogadro Hypothesis
blocks.contentMarkdown: Gay-Lussac's Law of Gaseous Volumes (1808) states that reacting gases combine or form products in simple whole-number volume ratios at identical temperature and pressure.

blocks.title: 2. Key Academic Principles: Gay-Lussac\'s Law and Avogadro Hypothesis
blocks.contentMarkdown: Avogadro's Law (1811) states that equal volumes of all gases under identical temperature and pressure contain equal numbers of molecules (V is proportional to n).

blocks.title: 3. Key Academic Principles: Gay-Lussac\'s Law and Avogadro Hypothesis
blocks.contentMarkdown: Avogadro distinguished between fundamental atoms and compound molecules, resolving Dalton's dilemma regarding fractional atoms.
